sections.html:
Columbia is South Carolina's capital and the seat of Richland County. Parts of the city spill into Lexington and Kershaw counties, so the first thing to settle is which county your parcel sits in. That decides which assessor, treasurer and register of deeds you deal with.

The city is near the middle of the state at the fall line, where the Broad and Saluda rivers join to form the Congaree. Anything close to those rivers deserves a flood zone check. Columbia was laid out as a planned capital in 1786, and burned in part in 1865, so one street can hold a historic bungalow and the next a postwar ranch. Condition and price vary block by block, and a citywide average tells you little.

Every residential rental in the city needs a Residential Rental Permit before a tenant moves in. The rule covers units rented after July 1, 2016, and permits expire each year on December 31.

  • Owners of up to 4 units use the nonbusiness form; owners of 5 or more use the business form.
  • Applications go to Code Enforcement at 920 Hemlock Drive, Columbia, SC 29201, and you pay online once approved.
  • Questions go to 803-545-4362.

Short-term rentals follow separate rules. An operator needs an STR Permit from Code Enforcement plus a Business License. Under Ordinance 2025-107, STRs are allowed in mixed-use, activity center and corridor, commercial and employment campus districts. In residential districts they are allowed on parcels fronting a four-lane arterial or collector street. An ordinance approved March 3, 2026 lets owner-occupied homes in residential districts operate without the four-lane condition. Details are on the city's STR page and the residential rentals page.

If you are selling a house with tenants, a current permit helps. A buyer or investor will ask for it, and a lapsed permit is a delay you can fix before listing.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
County governments levy and collect property tax in South Carolina. Bills for houses inside Columbia are based on values set by the Richland County Assessor. Payment is due between September 30 and January 15, and penalties stack up after that (Code sections 12-45-70 and 12-45-180).

If still unpaid byAdded penalty
After January 153 percent
February 2Another 7 percent
March 17Another 5 percent

Ask the treasurer for your notice date and amount, since they vary with the bill. If you sell during the year, tax owed is normally settled at closing from your proceeds.

To contest a value in Richland County, send the Assessor a written objection, online or in person, with documents that back up your number. The deadline is 90 days from the dated reassessment notice, or the first penalty date on the current bill, whichever comes first. Filing an appeal does not replace paying the bill.

If someone else files for you, they need a power of attorney on Form SC2848. An LLC owner should provide the company's organizing documents.

The Assessor's Office is at 2020 Hampton Street, Suite 2058, Columbia, SC 29204, phone 803-576-2640. The county's assessment appeal page has the online portal. A lower assessed value can help a future owner, but it rarely changes what a buyer will pay today, so weigh the effort against your sale date.

sections.h2: What buyers notice about a Columbia house
sections.html:
Summers are long and hot, so inspectors in Columbia look closely at air conditioning, attic ventilation and the roof. Anything near the Broad, Saluda or Congaree rivers should come with a flood zone determination.

Houses close to an interstate ramp or a rail line should be described honestly, because noise tends to come up at showings. Good road access, on the other hand, is a real plus for commuters.

sections.h2: Your options for a quick sale
sections.html:
A Columbia seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer. Houses near the university or downtown often draw investors. Houses that need work, or that have tenants in place, are harder to sell on the open market.

Here is how the paths differ in practice:

  • Listing with an agent: best for a house in good shape when you can wait through showings, inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Selling on your own: you save a commission but handle pricing, paperwork and negotiation yourself.
  • Cash offer: usually as-is, with no repair requests and no lender to wait on, and a closing date you can often pick.

Before you decide, gather four things: the permit status of any rental, the parcel's county, your tax bill and your mortgage payoff. They answer most questions a buyer or closing attorney will ask. At closing, the attorney pays off your loan and any taxes owed from the proceeds and records the deed.

sections.h2: What happens from offer to closing
sections.html:
The steps are the same whichever route you take, though the timing is not. First you agree on a price and sign a contract. Next the buyer does due diligence: an inspection, a title search and, with a mortgage, an appraisal. A cash buyer can often shorten or skip the appraisal and loan steps, which is where most delays come from.

Then a closing attorney prepares the deed and the settlement statement. On closing day you sign, the attorney pays your lender and any taxes still owed out of your proceeds, and the deed is recorded. You get what is left.

Bring a photo ID, your mortgage lender's name and loan number, keys and garage openers, and any rental leases and permit paperwork. If an heir or a co-owner is on the title, their signature is needed too, so line that up early. Selling a house with a lien or back taxes is still possible, since those debts are paid from the sale, but ask for payoff figures well before the closing date.

faqs.a: Mostly. Columbia is the Richland County seat, but parts of the city reach into Lexington and Kershaw counties. Confirm your parcel's county before you call an assessor or treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a rented house in Columbia?
faqs.a: The city requires a Residential Rental Permit for each rental unit, renewed every year by December 31. A buyer will want proof it is current. Code Enforcement can help at 803-545-4362.

faqs.q: When are Richland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due between September 30 and January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts after January 15. Ask the treasurer for the exact date and amount on your notice.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Columbia assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the dated reassessment notice, or until the first penalty date on the current bill if that comes first. An appeal does not stop the bill from coming due.

faqs.q: Can a buyer use a Columbia house as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Only where zoning and the city permit allow it. An STR Permit and a Business License are both required. In residential areas it depends on the street or on owner occupancy under the 2026 ordinance.
